# Intune Gotchas

> Known Microsoft Intune / endpoint-policy patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Azure VM Entra-ID RDP fails until Microsoft Remote Desktop has a tenant-wide consent grant for Azure Windows VM Sign-In](entra-vm-rdp-tenant-consent.md): Entra-joined Azure VMs by IP fail with "requested security package does not exist" / AADSTS50206 / AADSTS65002 because the Microsoft Remote Desktop -> Azure Windows VM Sign-In consent has never been granted in the tenant. The generic admin-consent URL fails on the app's legacy AAD Graph permission. Fix: targeted oauth2PermissionGrant for just the user_impersonation scope. Also names common red herrings (RCG, Lsa Security Packages, SYSTEM-context dsregcmd). HIGH.
- [Autodesk (ODIS) Win32 deploy: package the generated image, not the downloaded creator exe](autodesk-odis-win32-deploy.md): The ~30 MB Autodesk download is AdOdisDeployTool.exe (a creator), not the installer; run it to build the multi-GB image folder, then wrap that. Also: cert app-only Graph auth uploads Win32 LOB fine (content goes to the Azure SAS URI), and you need DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All. HIGH.
- [androidManagedStoreApp cannot be created via app-only/cert Graph -- approve in the Managed Google Play iframe](androidmanagedstoreapp-needs-iframe-approval.md): POSTing an androidManagedStoreApp returns 400 from the AppLifecycle service even with DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All and a bound MGP account; managed Google Play apps must be approved in the interactive Google iframe (which app-only auth can't drive), then they auto-sync and can be assigned via Graph. HIGH.
- [Intune mobileApp assignment fails until publishingState is 'published'](mobileapp-assignment-requires-published-state.md): A new store app starts in publishingState=processing; assigning before it flips to 'published' returns 400 "PublishingState is not Published". Poll the app first. Also covers the stray uninstall->All Devices assignment trap (uninstall wins conflicts and removes the app). HIGH.
- [A new iosStoreApp can wedge in publishingState=processing for an hour -- delete and recreate](iosstoreapp-stuck-processing-recreate.md): iosStoreApp usually publishes in 1-5 min but can stall for an hour+ on Microsoft's AppLifecycle backend; the definition/permissions are fine. Remediation: delete the unassigned app and recreate (guard on zero assignments), then poll the new id. MEDIUM.
- [win32LobApp create needs the unified `rules` collection, not the legacy `detectionRules`](win32lobapp-rules-not-detectionrules.md): The current AppLifecycle service (api-version 2025-07-02) silently ignores `detectionRules` + `win32LobApp*Detection` types and 400s with "must have at least one detection rule specified". Use `rules[]` of `win32LobApp*Rule` subtypes with a `ruleType` discriminator; also `minimumSupportedWindowsRelease` string replaces the min-OS object, and `displayVersion` drops silently. Diagnose by GET-ing a working app's `rules`. HIGH.
- [windowsMobileMSI content files require a base64 MobileMsiData manifest](windowsmobilemsi-content-file-requires-manifest.md): Win32 content files legitimately pass `manifest: null`, so Win32 upload code reused for an MSI LOB app 400s with "Invalid manifest: must not be null for the current app type". windowsMobileMSI needs base64 MobileMsiData XML (UpgradeCode read from the MSI Property table via WindowsInstaller.Installer COM). Error lands on the content-file POST, after the app already exists, so each retry strands a partial app. HIGH.
- [useDeviceContext must be OMITTED, not set to false, for a per-System-only MSI](usedevicecontext-must-be-omitted-not-false.md): "'UseDeviceContext' has been set on application, but MSI is not a dual-mode application" reads like a value problem, but Intune counts the property as set by its mere PRESENCE in the payload, so retrying with `$false` fails identically to `$true`. Omit the key entirely; declare machine context via MsiExecutionContext="System" in the manifest instead. HIGH.
